title: Why OOP concepts matter in development projects
answer: OOP concepts matter because they provide tools for controlling complexity as a codebase grows. Encapsulation protects invariants, abstraction creates stable contracts, inheritance can reuse genuinely shared behavior, polymorphism allows implementations to vary behind one interface, and composition assembles behavior without rigid inheritance. In AeroTopo these techniques keep product rules localized and make new product types easier to add and test. The value is maintainability and change isolation, not simply using classes everywhere.
